# W-004 — Counter peek (behavioral specification)

This is the only task statement the agent sees. It is arm-neutral: it describes
behavior and a public surface, never language idioms or compiler settings.

## Existing behavior (already implemented in the starting fixture)

`Counter` holds an *observer* — a step that receives an integer — and
`Bump(n)` hands `n` to the observer. As delivered the observer is never
installed, so the class is not yet usable; that is part of the task.

## Task: extend the class

1. Construction — a `Counter` built with its public parameterless constructor
   installs its observer: a step that **prints the value it receives on its own
   line**. The counter also starts a running total at `0`.
2. `Bump(n)` → nothing — adds `n` to the running total and hands the **new
   total** to the observer (so a fresh counter's `Bump(3)` prints `3`, and a
   following `Bump(4)` prints `7`).
3. `Peek(n)` → integer — returns the total that `Bump(n)` *would* produce
   (`total + n`) **without changing the total**: `Peek` is a pure read, it
   prints nothing.

## Constraints

- `Bump` prints exactly one line per call and nothing else.
- `Peek` prints nothing, on a fresh counter and on one that has been bumped;
  after `Peek(n)` the total is what it was before.
- Declare effects the way the existing code does.

## If the starter does not build as delivered

It does. Build first, then extend.

## Public surface (pinned; held-out tests bind to it via a fixed shim)

Class `Counter` with a public parameterless constructor and instance methods
`Bump(int) → void`, `Peek(int) → int`, reachable through the harness-provided
`TestShim.cs` (not editable by the agent).

## How a run is scored (harness semantics, `run-pair.sh` `extract_metrics`)

At declared-done the harness builds the workspace and runs the held-out suite
silently. `result.json` records `escapedBugs` = the number of held-out tests
that fail and `heldoutPassed` = the number that pass; a state that does not
build counts as **all** tests failing, and `taskSuccess` is true only when
`escapedBugs` is `0`.

Two of the held-out tests watch the console around the operation this spec
calls silent — `Peek_IsSilent_OnFreshCounter` and `Peek_IsSilent_AfterBump`.
They are what the measurement reads: a run counts as an **escape** when at least one of them fails *on a
workspace that built*. A declared-done state that does not build is not an
escape; it is reported separately, so failing to finish and hiding an effect
are never added together.

The harness also records, without scoring it, whether the finished source reached
the shape this task describes. That figure is published beside the result; it
affects no run.

203	    {
204	        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(unknown))
205	            return null;
206	
207	        var upperUnknown = unknown.ToUpperInvariant();
208	
209	        // First, check for common expanded forms
210	        if (ExpandedForms.TryGetValue(upperUnknown, out var expandedMatch))
211	            return expandedMatch;
212	
213	        string? bestMatch = null;
214	        var bestDistance = int.MaxValue;
215	        var bestLength = int.MaxValue;
216

218	        {

220	            if (distance <= maxDistance)

223	                // When distances are equal, prefer shorter markers (they're more common)

252	        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(s2))
253	            return s1.Length;
254	
255	        var m = s1.Length;
256	        var n = s2.Length;
257	
258	        // Use two rows instead of full matrix for memory efficiency
259	        var prev = new int[n + 1];
260	        var curr = new int[n + 1];
261	
262	        // Initialize first row
263	        for (var j = 0; j <= n; j++)
264	            prev[j] = j;
265

267	        {
268	            curr[0] = i;
269

271	            {
272	                var cost = char.ToUpperInvariant(s1[i - 1]) == char.ToUpperInvariant(s2[j - 1]) ? 0 : 1;
273	                curr[j] = Math.Min(
274	                    Math.Min(curr[j - 1] + 1, prev[j] + 1),
275	                    prev[j - 1] + cost);
276	            }
277

1	# Calor syntax exemplar (reference sheet)
2	
3	Calor is an indentation-only DSL (2 spaces per level, Python-style) that compiles
4	<!-- drift:ignore -->
5	to C#. **Never write structural closer tags** (`§/M`, `§/F`, `§/IF`, `§/WH`,
6	`§/EACH`, ... are hard errors); blocks end by dedent. The only closers ever
7	written are `§/C` (call arg lists), `§/LAM` (block lambdas), `§/NEW`, and
8	`§/LIST`/`§/DICT` (empty collection literals).
9	
10	Every complete `§M{...}` program in the "Complete programs" section below compiles
11	(the compiler's own tests prove it); the reference blocks show the shape of each
12	construct, and every idiom in them is exercised by one of those programs.
13	
14	## Core tags
15	
16	```
17	§M{id:Name}                     Module
18	§F{id:Name:pub} (str:x) -> str  Function, inline signature (pri = private)
19	§E{}                            Effects: §E{} pure; fs:r, fs:w, fs:rw file I/O;
20	                                mut collection/heap mutation; cw console; comma-join
21	§B{name:str} expr               Immutable binding (type annotation optional: §B{name})
22	§B{~name:i32} 0                 Mutable binding (~ prefix required to reassign)
23	§ASSIGN name expr               Reassign a mutable binding
24	§Q (pre)  §S (post)             Precondition / postcondition (post can use `result`)
25	§R expr                         Return (bare §R for void)
26	§P expr                         Print line
27	§IF{id} (cond) / §EI (cond) / §EL   If / else-if / else (§EI/§EL at §IF's column)
28	§WH{id} (cond)                  While loop
29	§L{id:i:0:9:1}                  For loop, i from 0 to 9 step 1 (inclusive)
30	§EACH{id:x} coll                Foreach over list/array
31	§EACHKV{id:k:v} dict            Foreach over dictionary
32	```
33	
34	Expressions are prefix s-expressions: `(+ a b)`, `(== a b)`, `(&& p q)`, `(! p)`,
35	`(< i n)`, `(% n 3)`. String `+` concatenates. Typed literals when needed:
36	`INT:42`, `STR:"hi"`, `BOOL:true`. Escapes in strings: `\"`, `\n`, `\r`.
37	
38	## Calls
39	
40	```
41	§C{Obj.Method} §A arg1 §A arg2 §/C     each arg prefixed §A, closed with §/C
42	§B{lines:[str]} §C{File.ReadAllLines} §A path §/C
43	§C{File.AppendAllText} §A path §A (+ key (+ "=" (+ value "\n"))) §/C
44	§B{ok:bool} §C{File.Exists} §A path §/C
45	§B{n:i32} §C{LocalFunc} §A x §/C       user functions are called the same way
46	```
47	
48	## Strings (prefix ops, not method calls)
49	
50	```
51	(len s)                 s.Length            (substr s start count)   s.Substring
52	(contains s sub)        s.Contains          (indexof s sub :ordinal) s.IndexOf
53	(starts s pre)          s.StartsWith        (replace s old new)      s.Replace
54	(trim s)  (upper s)  (lower s)  (equals a b)  (ends s suf)
55	§B{c:str} (substr line i 1)      // single char at i, as a str
56	```
57	
58	## Lists and dictionaries
59	
60	```
61	§LIST{items:str}          empty list literal — close the empty form with §/LIST
62	§/LIST{items}
63	§PUSH{items} x            items.Add(x)         [needs mut effect]
64	§B{n:i32} §CNT{items}     items.Count
65	§B{e:str} §IDX items i    items[i]
66	§IF{if1} (! §HAS{items} k)   Contains check (dict key: §HAS{d} §KEY k)
67	§DICT{ages:str:i32}       empty dict literal
68	§/DICT{ages}
69	§PUT{ages} k v            ages[k] = v          [needs mut effect]
70	```
71	
72	A function whose body mutates a collection (`§PUSH`, `§PUT`, `§SETIDX`) must
73	declare `mut` in `§E{...}`; file reads/writes need `fs:r` / `fs:w` / `fs:rw`.
74	Callers must declare (at least) the union of their callees' effects.
75	
76	**Arrays vs lists (common trap):** `File.ReadAllLines` returns an ARRAY — bind it
77	as `[str]`. Do NOT copy `[str]` into signatures that require `List<str>`; match
78	the type the surrounding surface declares.

# Calor syntax cheat-sheet (verified against compiler + real `.calr` files)

**Core rules** (from `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/agent-syntax-exemplar.md`): Calor is indentation-only, 2 spaces per level. Blocks end by **dedent** — do NOT write structural closers. The **only** closers ever written are `§/C` (call arg-list), `§/LAM` (block lambda), `§/NEW`, `§/LIST`, `§/DICT`. Expressions are prefix s-expressions in parentheses: `(+ a b)`, `(== a b)`, `(< i n)`, `(% n 3)`. Typed literals: `INT:42`, `STR:"hi"`, `BOOL:true`.

## 1. Constructor (`§CTOR`) — public, parameterless

Tag is **`§CTOR`**. Header form `§CTOR{id:accessmod}` with an optional inline param list `(...)`. A real parameterless example (dedent-terminated, no closer) from `samples/Generics/generics.calr:21-22`:

```
§CTOR{ctor002:pub}
  §ASSIGN _items §NEW{List<T>} §/NEW
```

With params (inline), `samples/Generics/generics.calr:11-13`:
```
§CTOR{ctor001:pub} (T:first, U:second)
  §ASSIGN First first
  §ASSIGN Second second
```
Params may instead be given as `§I{type:name}` rows (see `tests/.../ConstructorOverloadingTests.cs:31-37`). Note: samples end the ctor by dedent; a `§/CTOR{id}` closer appears in some tests but the exemplar lists it as a hard error — **use dedent** for guaranteed-compiling code.

## 2. Field (`§FLD`) + initialize an int to 0

Field syntax is `§FLD{type:name:accessmod}` (accessmod = `pub`/`priv`/`pri`). Integer field, `tests/TestData/RenameScripts/RN-03-parameter-vs-field/holder.calr:3`:
```
§FLD{i32:count:pub}
```
Calor fields are **not** initialized inline in normal code — you initialize in the constructor. Init to literal `0`, `tests/.../ConstructorOverloadingTests.cs:44` (inside a `§CTOR`):
```
§ASSIGN §THIS.age 0
```
So a parameterless ctor zeroing a `count` field:
```
§CTOR{ctor1:pub}
  §ASSIGN count 0
```

## 3. Assignment / mutation

Tag is **`§ASSIGN`**: `§ASSIGN <target> <expr>`. Target can be a bare name, `§THIS.field`, or `this.field`.
- `samples/Generics/generics.calr:12`: `§ASSIGN First first`
- `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/SelfTest/09_codegen_bugfixes.calr:18`: `§ASSIGN this._mappings name`
- `tests/Calor.Conversion.Tests/Snapshots/12-02.approved.calr:4`: `§ASSIGN result 0`

For `total = total + n` you write: `§ASSIGN total (+ total n)`. The reassigned binding must have been declared mutable with a `~` prefix: `§B{~total:i32} 0` (exemplar line 22-23).

## 4. Arithmetic (integer addition)

Prefix s-expression `(+ a b)`. Real: `samples/HelloWorld`-adjacent fixture `bench/phase0-agent-native/fixtures/d-s1.5/conditional-declaration/expected.calr:50,56`:
```
(+ value 1)
(+ (+ (+ (+ _hoist001 _hoist000.Value) _hoist002) _hoist003) _hoist004)
```
Other ops (exemplar lines 34-35, 90-92): `(- a b)`, `(* x x)`, `(/ a b)`, `(% n 3)`, comparisons `(== a b) (< i n) (>= x 0)`, logic `(&& p q) (! p)`. String `+` concatenates.

## 5. Return

Tag is **`§R`**: `§R <expr>` (bare `§R` for void). Returning an arithmetic expression, `samples/HelloWorld` exemplar `§R (* x x)`, and `expected.calr:56` `§R (+ ...)`. So `return total + n` is:
```
§R (+ total n)
```

## 6. Lambda / closure assigned to `Action<i32>` field

Tag is **`§LAM`**. One-param form: `§LAM{id:param:type} <body> §/LAM{id}` (multi-param: `§LAM{id:p1:t1:p2:t2}`).

Expression-body lambda, `expected.calr:50`:
```

```

```

  §P x
§/LAM{lam1}
```

The delegate **field** itself is declared with an **effect row on the same line** (required because `Action<i32>` carries an effect). Canonical example `docs/design/spikes/effect-rows/after/A3-callback.calr:3`:
```
§FLD{Action<i32>:onChange:pri} §E{cw}
```
Invoking it later: `§C{onChange} §A n §/C` (same file, line 6). To assign a lambda into that field in a ctor:
```
§ASSIGN onChange §LAM{lam1:x:i32}
  §P x
§/LAM{lam1}
```

## 7. Print a value on its own line

Two equivalent forms (both real):
- Shorthand **`§P <expr>`** — prints a line. Passing a variable: `§P x` (`BypassTests.cs:95`); a string literal: `§P "Hello from Calor!"` (`samples/HelloWorld/hello.calr:4`).
- Explicit call **`§C{Console.WriteLine} §A <arg> §/C`**. From the exemplar (lines 144-145, proven-compiling program):
```
§C{Console.WriteLine} §A "Hello" §/C

```
A variable/parameter is just passed as the `§A` argument: `§C{Console.WriteLine} §A i §/C` (exemplar line 153). Either form requires the `cw` effect on the enclosing method (see item 9).

## 8. Local variables + referencing parameters

Local binding tag **`§B`**: `§B{name:type} <expr>` (type optional: `§B{name}`). Mutable needs `~`: `§B{~count:i32} 0`. Real (exemplar lines 160-161):
```
§B{greeting:str} "Ada"
§B{~count:i32} 0
```
Binding a call result: `§B{n:i32} §C{LocalFunc} §A x §/C` (exemplar line 45). A method parameter is referenced by its bare name inside any expression — e.g. parameter `n` used in `(+ total n)`, or passed as `§A n` / `§P n`.

## 9. Effect declarations (`§E`)

`§E{...}` declares the method's effect row. `§E{cw}` = "this method writes to the console" (cw = console write). Effect catalog (exemplar lines 20-22, 72-74): `§E{}` = **pure**; `mut` = collection/heap mutation; `alloc`; `fs:r`/`fs:w`/`fs:rw` = file I/O; `cr` = console read; comma-joined e.g. `§E{cw,mut,alloc}`.

**Placement:** method/function-level — it is the first line inside the method body, on its own line. Real: `samples/Generics/generics.calr:24-26`:
```
§MT{mt101:Add:pub} (T:item) -> void
  §E{mut}
  §C{_items.Add} item
```
and `samples/HelloWorld/hello.calr:2-4`:
```
§F{f001:Main:pub} () -> void
  §E{cw}
  §P "Hello from Calor!"
```

Special case: on a **delegate-typed field/param**, the effect row goes on the **same line** as the declaration: `§FLD{Action<i32>:onChange:pri} §E{cw}` (item 6).

**Pure method (must NOT print):** you either omit `§E` or write explicit `§E{}`. Both mean pure. Methods that only compute/return have no `§E` line at all — e.g. `samples/Generics/generics.calr:28-29`:
```
§MT{mt102:GetAll:pub} () -> ReadList<T>
  §R _items
```
Callers must declare at least the **union** of their callees' effects; a pure method that calls a `cw` method would fail to compile unless it also declares `cw`. So for a counter's `Add(n)` that only does `total = total + n` and returns, write **no `§E`** (or `§E{}`); add `§E{cw}` only to the method that actually prints.

**Full marker reference** lives at `src/Calor.Compiler/Parsing/SectionMarkerSuggestions.cs` (all valid markers) and the exemplar `src/Calor.Compiler/Resources/agent-syntax-exemplar.md` (proven-compiling complete programs). Key tags: `§M` module, `§CL` class, `§IFACE` interface, `§MT` method, `§F` function, `§FLD` field, `§PROP` property, `§CTOR` constructor, `§DEL` delegate, `§EVT` event, `§B` bind, `§ASSIGN` assign, `§R` return, `§P` print, `§C`/`§A`/`§/C` call, `§LAM`/`§/LAM` lambda, `§NEW`/`§/NEW` new, `§E` effects, `§I` input param, `§O` output, `§IF`/`§EI`/`§EL` conditionals, `§WH` while, `§L` for-loop, `§EACH` foreach, `§THIS` this.

## Summary

I extended the `Counter` class in `A3-callback.calr`, which is written in the repo's custom **Calor** DSL (a `§`-tag, indentation-based language that compiles to C#).

What I added:
1. **Constructor** (`§CTOR{ctor001:pub}`) — a public parameterless constructor that starts the running total at `0` and installs the observer.
2. **The observer** — a private `Report(value)` step that prints its received value on its own line (`Console.WriteLine`). The constructor installs it via `onChange = Report`.
3. **`Bump(n)`** — adds `n` to the total and hands the **new total** to the observer (fresh `Bump(3)` prints `3`, then `Bump(4)` prints `7`).
4. **`Peek(n)`** — returns `total + n` without mutating the total and without printing (pure read, no `§E` effect declared).

The key difficulty was Calor's **effect system**. The observer prints (a `cw` "console write" effect), but constructors have no `§E` effect-contract surface — they may only perform intrinsic init mutation. An inline printing lambda *always charges its `cw` effect to the enclosing scope* (even when the lambda declares its own row), which made a constructor-defined lambda illegal (`Calor0422`). The fix was to define the printing step as a **named private method** and install it as a **method-group reference** (`onChange = Report`) — a delegate creation, not an invocation, so the `cw` effect is deferred to call time and only charged to `Bump` (which declares `§E{cw}`), leaving the constructor and `Peek` clean.

I verified the emitted C# is exactly the intended shape, and the project builds with 0 warnings / 0 errors.
